description: Integrate and review PR targets through the shared local repair batch, then reconcile applicable whole-story proof and closeout.

steps.label: Review PR Candidates And Repair Valid Findings
Run PR Feedback Through Existing Review Batch Gates
Reply To Findings After Disposition And Repair
Repeat Only For Useful Review Of A Changed Candidate
steps.question: Read-only: identify this PR review invocation and current round from the running pr_review_current_plan conversation. GET /conversations returns items and nextCursor: inspect the parent flags.flow.loopStack and flags.flow.subflowWaveProgress.jobs, including the pr_review_batch:local_review_batch instanceId and conversationId; match the child by conversationId, flowName and flags.flowChild executionId, instanceId and waveInvocationId. Read the child flags.flow.values.review_batch_targets from GET /conversations and its terminal, status and terminalOutcome from GET /flows/runs/{conversationId}; that endpoint does not return flags. Bind the actual current wave and child to its immutable batch and active cycle, cross-checking batch-launch.md and job.md instance IDs beginning pr_target_reviews:. If either API lookup is unavailable, use independently attributable exact current-batch launch, snapshot, gates, disposition, completed-fix records, outcome, PR reply assessment and fresh target Git evidence when sufficient; never substitute an older batch or guess identity. Preserve missing or partial coverage as incomplete. A fix-bearing HEAD must contain an attributable source or test Git commit and remote review must be pinned to the exact pushed HEAD. Read the current batch target snapshot, applicable gates and dispositions, repair evidence, outcome and PR reply assessment, then current Git HEAD for each target. Return exact JSON only: {"answer":"yes"} or {"answer":"no"}. Answer no for a verified new committed fix-bearing HEAD needing pinned remote review when safe publication and observation are available. Also answer no for a newly arrived potential-issue source comment requiring disposition, including one ultimately rejected or duplicate, when it has not yet had its one same-head gates-only pass. Reuse the existing launch in that pass: no request, push or description refresh. An existing authoritative applicable disposition permits the reply owner to answer a late duplicate directly. Never repeat the same comment's gates-only pass, reopen disposed or exhausted findings without material new evidence, or repeat an unchanged candidate's launch. Failed or ambiguous posting, missing evidence, and unchanged unavailable coverage do not justify repeating; preserve uncertainty for settlement rather than claiming clean coverage. A changed candidate invalidates old clean coverage; independently useful changed targets must still be processed. Check the current batch markdown outcome and codeInfoTmp/reviews/<review_wave_id>-parallel-automated.json against the exact wave, cycle, target snapshot, candidate and actual check outcomes. A clean settlement requires clear review and actual successful applicable automated validation tied to the same current candidate. A changed fix-bearing candidate requires another review and validation round when safe. Failed, skipped, unavailable, ambiguous, missing or mismatched validation remains incomplete; do not retry an unchanged failure. Honor selected story and testing exclusions. A same-head gates-only pass reuses applicable validation evidence and does not launch validation again.

content: Read and apply $CODEINFO_ROOT/codeinfo_markdown/local_review_closeout.md where applicable. Independently reconcile every actual PR wave and immutable batch, exact pushed PR-reviewed heads, reviewer coverage, reply and disposition assessments, patch and test evidence, verified and unverified fixes, pending findings, and applicable whole-story proof. Establish each round from the running PR flow wave/child outcomes and immutable batch job instances beginning pr_target_reviews:, not the latest-batch pointer; retain unknown coverage when association cannot be established. Reconcile missing completed-fix tasks only as the existing local closeout rules permit. Account for integration and all review rounds since the last applicable proof, owned dirty or reverted source/test changes where established, and proof outcomes under the selected story and testing restrictions. If final proof changes source or tests after an exact PR review, retain that candidate as unreviewed and review coverage incomplete. Preserve per-provider refusal, quota and failure alongside useful sibling findings; a terminal provider decline alone does not force the cycle incomplete. Preserve original open work, existing parent-consumed results, human-pending proof and all uncertainty; do not create deferred tasks or blocker records, launch another review or proof, commit or push.

Settle the existing active final review cycle using the current cycle ID and scripts/record_review_cycle_outcome.py: record completed only when trustworthy evidence establishes the PR pass is fully settled with exact-head coverage, dispositions, replies, verified repairs and applicable proof; otherwise record incomplete with a precise reason. If settlement is unavailable, report it honestly. Do not initialize another cycle.

Reconcile the applicable batch markdown outcome and codeInfoTmp/reviews/<review_wave_id>-parallel-automated.json against the exact wave, cycle, target snapshot, candidate and actual check outcomes. Require clear exact-head review coverage and actual successful applicable automated validation tied to that same candidate. Reconcile every changed fix-bearing candidate and preserve missing, failed, skipped, unavailable, ambiguous or mismatched validation as incomplete; same-head gates-only passes reuse applicable validation evidence. Honor story and testing exclusions and preserve manual proof restrictions and outcomes separately. The removed post-review whole-story proof child is not expected.

Reconcile each reported failure, skipped check and evidence gap against the current requirements, source and later applicable evidence. Treat it as outstanding only if it still applies and has not been resolved or superseded. Clearly distinguish a confirmed current failure from historical results and missing or unavailable proof; do not describe an evidence gap as a confirmed defect or an unperformed check as passed.
